content.title: About
content.content: Leeks (Allium ampeloprasum var. porrum) are a perennial vegetable from the onion family. The plant produces long, flat leaves that form a thick, white "stem". The flavor is mild, slightly sweet, and aromatic. Leeks are eaten raw, boiled, roasted, and are a staple in soups, salads, and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Leeks belong to the same species group as common onion, garlic, and shallots.
In ancient Rome, leeks were a symbol of strength and were used for medicinal purposes.
The leek stalk is made of multiple layered leaves that create its characteristic tube shape.
In Russia, leeks are traditionally grown in open fields and greenhouses, while in Japan they are often featured in the dish "nama-edama".
Leeks contain more vitamin K than most other vegetables.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K plays a key role in blood clotting and supports bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and sulfur compounds help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to alliums
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to leeks, including itching, swelling, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs or irritable bowel syndrome may experience gas and bloating after eating leeks.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Leeks contain small amounts of oxalates, which can be a concern for those prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Leeks can be added to soups, stews, casseroles, salads, and used as a filling for pies. The white part of the stalk is usually cooked, while the green leaves can be added to stocks or used as a garnish. Before cooking, rinse thoroughly to remove sand trapped between the layers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leeks in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a plastic bag or placed in a container with a small amount of moisture. When stored properly, they stay fresh for up to two weeks. Keep them away from fruit, as they can accelerate fruit spoilage.
